changelog: Recommendations now understand what language something is in, which is the change most likely to be visible on your home screen. Until now the engine never learned the original language of anything in your library - Jellyfin does not supply it and the enricher that could fetch it skipped library titles entirely - so a Hindi film and an American one in the same genre looked identical to the recommender, and personal discovery searched a global popularity list that English-language releases win. Language is now backfilled onto library titles, written into the text the recommender reads, and learned as a preference; personal discovery runs a second pass restricted to the languages you actually watch, with a vote threshold that does not quietly exclude most of a national cinema. A new Import all watch history button on the Users page backfills every account's taste profile from the play history Jellyfin already had. Live capture only ever saw what happened after the plugin was installed, so profiles started empty on a server with years of viewing. The import reads played state, play count, favourites and ratings for every title, keeps the original dates so recent viewing still counts for more, shows per-user progress, and is safe to run more than once. Behaviour retention has been removed. It defaulted to 400 days and, less visibly, was permanently deleting older events every fifteen minutes - which would have destroyed an imported history shortly after it arrived. The engine now keeps everything and lets the existing 90-day decay decide what still matters. A new Embeddings page shows which model is actually producing your content vectors rather than which one is selected, and a Test provider button proves it works instead of waiting for it to fail: it embeds three short texts and checks that two related ones score closer together than an unrelated one, so a provider that answers successfully with meaningless vectors is caught. Standing problems now appear as a red banner on every Observatory page until they are fixed, instead of a log line nobody was watching for. Content vectors are now saved to the database, so a restart reuses them instead of re-embedding the whole catalogue. Only new or edited titles cost a call, and the catalogue is embedded in bounded batches with retries rather than one large request. IMPORTANT, ACTION REQUIRED: the built-in TF-IDF provider has been removed and Ollama is the new default. TF-IDF compared word overlap rather than meaning and could not be mixed with a real model's vectors. Install Ollama, run 'ollama pull nomic-embed-text', then set the Ollama URL under Settings, Embeddings and press Test provider. Until a provider answers, More Like This and the taste blend on the trending row will be inactive; your watch history, taste profiles and everything driven by them are unaffected. This is a beta release.
